objectives.en: Explain the causes of the 1991 crisis
Distinguish stabilisation and structural reform measures

narration.en: Imagine a family that has money for only two weeks of groceries and owes money everywhere. In 1991 India's foreign exchange position looked like that.
narration.kn: ಕೇವಲ ಎರಡು ವಾರಗಳ ದಿನಸಿಗೆ ಹಣವಿದ್ದು ಎಲ್ಲೆಡೆ ಸಾಲ ಇರುವ ಕುಟುಂಬವನ್ನು ಊಹಿಸಿ. 1991ರಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾರತದ ವಿದೇಶಿ ವಿನಿಮಯ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ಹಾಗೆಯೇ ಇತ್ತು.

body.en: The crisis of 1991 came from the inefficient management of the economy in the 1980s. Government spending exceeded revenue and borrowing was spent on current needs, not on productive investment. Exports did not grow fast enough to pay for imports, and foreign exchange reserves fell to a level that could finance imports for only about two weeks. Prices of essential goods rose sharply.
body.kn: 1980ರ ದಶಕದ ಅದಕ್ಷ ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ನಿರ್ವಹಣೆಯೇ 1991ರ ಬಿಕ್ಕಟ್ಟಿಗೆ ಕಾರಣ. ಸರ್ಕಾರದ ವೆಚ್ಚ ಆದಾಯವನ್ನು ಮೀರಿತು; ಸಾಲವನ್ನು ಉತ್ಪಾದಕ ಹೂಡಿಕೆಗೆ ಬಳಸಲಿಲ್ಲ. ವಿದೇಶಿ ವಿನಿಮಯ ಮೀಸಲು ಎರಡು ವಾರಗಳ ಆಮದಿಗೆ ಮಾತ್ರ ಸಾಕಾಗುವಷ್ಟು ಕುಸಿಯಿತು.

title.en: New Economic Policy: two kinds of measures

body.en: India received a loan of about $7 billion from the World Bank and the IMF and announced the New Economic Policy (NEP) in 1991. Stabilisation measures are short-term: they correct the balance of payments and control inflation. Structural reform measures are long-term: they improve efficiency by removing rigidities in the economy. Together these are called LPG: liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation.
body.kn: ಭಾರತ ವಿಶ್ವ ಬ್ಯಾಂಕ್ ಮತ್ತು ಐಎಂಎಫ್‌ನಿಂದ ಸುಮಾರು 7 ಬಿಲಿಯನ್ ಡಾಲರ್ ಸಾಲ ಪಡೆದು 1991ರಲ್ಲಿ ನೂತನ ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ನೀತಿ ಪ್ರಕಟಿಸಿತು. ಸ್ಥಿರೀಕರಣ ಕ್ರಮಗಳು ಅಲ್ಪಾವಧಿ; ರಚನಾತ್ಮಕ ಸುಧಾರಣಾ ಕ್ರಮಗಳು ದೀರ್ಘಾವಧಿ.

points.en: Stabilisation: short-term, balance of payments and inflation
Structural reform: long-term, efficiency and competitiveness

problem.en: A country's foreign exchange reserves are $1.2 billion and its imports cost $30 billion a year. For about how many weeks can the reserves pay for imports?

steps.en: This is the kind of situation India faced in 1991.

answer.en: About 2 weeks of imports: a balance of payments crisis.
